Subject: Private VPC / On-prem Architecture Review — next steps

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from our discovery: Acme wants a Private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) for inference workloads that keeps model artifacts off public cloud storage, supports customer KMS, and meets your SOC 2/ISO requirements. You mentioned a spike in traffic for peak hours and a desire to limit cross-region egress.

Next step: schedule a focused architecture review with our engineering team to walk your infra folks through the network considerations, KMS integration, and the on-prem packaging options. Proposed attendees:
- Jane Doe (Acme Infra)
- 1-2 members from Acme networking/security
- Nikhil Sharma (Redwood Systems Engineer)
- Myself (Aditya Rao)

Proposed times (PDT):
- Tue May 14, 10:00-11:00
- Wed May 15, 14:00-15:00
- Thu May 16, 09:00-10:00

Attached is a short pre-read (redwood-private-architecture-pre-read.pdf) that summarizes typical VPC topologies and the information we usually ask for ahead of a deep dive (network CIDRs, proxy/firewall rules, KMS provider). Could you confirm which slot works or share availability and the names/emails of the infra folks who should join?

If you prefer, I can send a calendar invite once you confirm a time.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Hi Jane —

Thanks — Wed May 15, 14:00 PDT works for me. I'll be there to cover network/firewall requirements, KMS integration patterns (AWS KMS / customer HSM), and options for on-prem packaging (container vs. VM image).

Quick checklist of items that would help us run a targeted 60-minute review: 
- VPC CIDR ranges and overlapping peering expectations
- Existing NAT / proxy / egress IP constraints
- Firewall rules (required outbound ports: 443 to Redwood control plane endpoints; optional ports for metrics/monitoring)
- KMS provider details (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM)
- Approx concurrent inference QPS and peak tokens per second (rough estimate)
- Preferred logging/audit retention and where logs should be shipped (S3, SIEM)

Attaching a simple network diagram we received from another customer for reference (acme-network-diagram-v1.png).

I'll assemble a short slide deck to use during the call and can share it ahead if you'd like.

Thanks,
